messages.text: Morning John. I reviewed your initial description and think the angle on cost/privacy is actually the strongest part of the story.
But for a workshop, I need to know exactly how you are evaluating this. Are we just looking at accuracy, or do you have baselines?
Good question. Right now it's mostly heuristic + a few spot checks, but I agree that's weak for a paper.
I'm thinking about comparing our local qwen2.5-14b against a standard API baseline to quantify the latency/privacy trade-off properly.
That would be very compelling. If you can show that the local model gets within a few percent of the cloud version while keeping data on-prem, that is a solid contribution.
Yeah, I think we can pull that off. Noor is building out the eval set right now so we have a fixed dataset for testing.
Please ensure that dataset includes ambiguous or edge-case interests, not just clear keywords. The 'why it failed' cases are often more interesting than the successes.
Noted. I'll make sure to highlight the adjudication failures in the one-pager too. Thanks, Sofia, this is helping a lot.
